producer.summary: Distillery bills it as a four-grain bourbon with a balanced mash bill, the official spirit of the 2017 and 2024 total solar eclipses, made in limited quantities. No nose/palate/finish notes on the page.

critics.nose: Caramel, fresh raspberry, prune, Concord grape and brown sugar.
critics.palate: Vanilla and caramel with light clove and white pepper.
critics.finish: Butterscotch, burnt orange peel and rye spice.
critics.summary: 2024 release reviewed (listed as 2 yrs 6 mos, 100 proof). Approachable, fun commemorative branding, but fairly simple given its youth. Rated 2.5 on Breaking Bourbon's own rating scale (scale not captured).

critics.nose: Plenty of graham cracker plus a touch of honey, turning sweeter and almost floral toward the back.
critics.palate: Bitter orange and orange peel develop over a honeyed base, moving toward tannin.
critics.finish: Tannic and dry with a sweet honeyed lift and a slight oiliness that softens the mouthfeel for a young whiskey.
critics.summary: Young 100-proof bourbon; reviewer scored it 7/10 at about $48.

notes: Input age 'At least 4 years' conflicts with producer ('minimum 2 years') and Breaking Bourbon (2y6m); age set from producer. Producer page has no tasting notes. A WhiskyCast rating page (89, dated Nov 2023, 2 yrs) was excluded: its date predates the 2024 release so batch (possibly 2017) is unclear and scale was not explicit.

producer.palate: Smooth and balanced with brown sugar, vanilla and gentle spice.
producer.summary: Notes relayed by retailer Wooden Cork and attributed there to the distillery; Kentucky straight small-batch bourbon from Master Distiller Arlon Casey Jones. Proof not stated on the page.

notes: Could not confirm a 90-proof Casey Jones Small Batch. Other Small Batch releases found were different proofs and excluded: 2019 first release at 104.2 proof (Distillery Trail) and a 108-proof bottling (People's Bourbon Review). Current distillery small-batch product is Revere at 100 proof, also excluded. Retailer notes may not match the 90-proof bottle.

Distillery's Barrel Cut line (Single Barrel 100-115 proof, Double Barrel 80-117 proof) is described as a corn-and-cane Kentucky specialty spirit, not bourbon, and no 90-proof Barrel Cut bourbon was found. Possible data error in input; nothing recorded.

producer.nose: Citrus, cedar and honeysuckle over balanced spicy oak.
producer.palate: Caramel and toasted oak first, then fruit, floral and oak notes.
producer.finish: Sweet citrus, floral and sweet oak play against dry cocoa, cinnamon and spicy oak.
producer.summary: Producer stresses it is distilled in-house (never sourced), sweet mash, barrel proof with no water added, and not chill-filtered.

notes: Producer page states barrel proof but no specific proof/age; batch proof varies so input 109 not verified. No critic review fetched (tool quota exhausted).

producer.nose: Sweet oak with orange zest and cedar, then tobacco and herbs.
producer.palate: Honeyed sweetness shifting quickly to cinnamon and spicy oak, with leather adding earthiness and a big body.
producer.finish: Viscous, with sweet toasted oak and dry cocoa.
producer.summary: Matured in two separate barrels for two full barrel extractions; bottled at barrel proof.

critics.nose: Medium-roast coffee, semi-sweet chocolate and cherry, plus brown sugar, torched orange peel and black tea.
critics.palate: Dark brown sugar and cacao up front, a flash of orange and cherry syrup, then burnt toffee and vanilla bean.
critics.finish: Chocolate-orange with growing orange oil, lingering vanilla, and cardamom, clove and nutmeg.
critics.summary: Batch 15CS241C6 (2022) at 54.2% ABV. Reviewer admired it more than enjoyed it, calling it frustratingly close to great, and questioned value at about $87. No numeric score captured.

facts.cask: Matured in two separate barrels (double oak)

notes: Barrel-proof product; proof varies by batch. Critic batch was 54.2% ABV (108.4 proof) vs input 109. Excluded a Bourbon Culture review (7.7/10) because it covered a 108-proof single-barrel store pick, not the standard release.
